Often used to describe procedures or processes (e.g., 'Nuclear waste must be disposed of') [6].
Active sentences with subjects like 'people' or 'someone' are more common in informal contexts [6].
In formal contexts, passives are used to avoid mentioning the agent [6].
We prefer to put the topic (what is being talked about) at the beginning of the sentence [6].
It is more normal to use an it-clause (e.g., 'It was believed that...') as the subject of a passive [6].
Some verbs have related nouns that can act as subjects (e.g., 'The installation... will be completed') [6].
